question: A 36-year-old woman with systemic lupus erythematosus (ANA 1:640, anti-dsDNA+), pancytopenia, no palpable splenomegaly, WHO Grade MF-2 reticulin fibrosis, non-clustered normolobated megakaryocytes, polyclonal lymphoid aggregates, and negative JAK2/CALR/MPL and extended myeloid NGS is referred for marrow fibrosis management. What is the appropriate first-line therapy?

choices.A: Immunosuppressive therapy (corticosteroids with steroid-sparing MMF or rituximab) for reversible Autoimmune Myelofibrosis (AIMF)
choices.B: Immediate myeloablative allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation for high-risk TN-PMF
choices.C: Frontline full-dose ruxolitinib 20 mg BID to eradicate a clonal JAK2 V617F stem cell pool
choices.D: Weekly therapeutic phlebotomy to target hematocrit <45%

rationale: SLE-associated AIMF presents with autoantibodies, non-clustered normolobated megakaryocytes, polyclonal lymphoid aggregates, and absent myeloid driver mutations; corticosteroids, MMF, or rituximab achieve 74-80% hematologic and reticulin resolution (PMID:38342652, PMID:33054116, PMID:24767860).

question: An untransfused patient with hyperinflammatory Myelofibrosis has hemoglobin 8.2 g/dL, serum ferritin 1,300 ng/mL, low serum iron, low TIBC, and transferrin saturation (TSAT) 12%. Which mechanism explains the combination of high ferritin and low TSAT?

choices.A: Bi-allelic HAMP deletion causing uncontrolled intestinal iron absorption and TSAT >90%
choices.B: Elevated IL-6 and BMP6/ACVR1 signaling upregulate hepatic HAMP (hepcidin), which degrades SLC40A1 (ferroportin) and traps iron inside reticuloendothelial macrophages while restricting iron delivery to erythroid precursors
choices.C: Direct binding of mutant CALR to circulating transferrin in peripheral blood
choices.D: Excessive renal urinary iron excretion caused by ruxolitinib

rationale: Inflammatory IL-6/STAT3 and BMP6/ACVR1 signaling elevate hepatic HAMP (hepcidin), causing internalization and degradation of SLC40A1 (ferroportin) on macrophages and enterocytes. This produces high serum ferritin with low serum iron/TSAT and functional iron-restricted anemia (PMID:36720133, NCT04173494).

question: Why do first-generation Type I JAK2 inhibitors such as ruxolitinib cause dose-limiting anemia and thrombocytopenia in JAK2 V617F+ Myelofibrosis patients?

choices.A: Ruxolitinib binds exclusively to mutant Phe617 in the JH2 domain and spares wild-type JAK2
choices.B: Ruxolitinib covalently destroys mature circulating red blood cells in the spleen
choices.C: Ruxolitinib targets the conserved JH1 catalytic ATP-binding hinge (Glu930/Leu932), which is identical in wild-type JAK2 and JAK2 V617F—equipotently blocking wild-type JAK2 signaling downstream of EPOR and MPL required for normal erythropoiesis and thrombopoiesis
choices.D: Ruxolitinib blocks extracellular TPO binding to MPL on megakaryocytes

rationale: Val617Phe resides in the regulatory JH2 pseudokinase domain (PDB:4FVQ/4FVR), whereas Type I JAK inhibitors bind the identical JH1 ATP-binding site (PDB:3KRR) in both mutant and wild-type JAK2, suppressing obligatory wild-type EPOR and MPL signaling (NCT00952289).

question: Which FDA-approved JAK inhibitor was specifically evaluated and approved for Myelofibrosis patients presenting with severe baseline thrombocytopenia (platelets <50 x 10^9/L) based on the Phase 3 PERSIST-2 trial?

choices.D: Pacritinib 200 mg BID (PERSIST-2, NCT02055781), a JAK1-sparing JAK2/IRAK1/ACVR1 inhibitor

rationale: Unlike COMFORT-I (platelets >=100 x 10^9/L) and JAKARTA (platelets >=50 x 10^9/L), PERSIST-2 (NCT02055781) enrolled severely thrombocytopenic MF patients (<50 x 10^9/L), supporting pacritinib's FDA approval at full 200 mg BID dosing via JAK1-sparing JAK2/IRAK1/ACVR1 inhibition.

question: Under the US Orphan Drug Act, what statutory US patient prevalence threshold qualifies Primary Myelofibrosis (ORPHA:824; ~15,000-25,000 US patients) for FDA Orphan Drug Designation, and how many years of US orphan market exclusivity does approval confer?

choices.A: Fewer than 200,000 US patients, conferring 7 years of indication-specific US orphan market exclusivity upon approval
choices.B: Fewer than 5,000 US patients, conferring 3 years of US orphan market exclusivity
choices.C: Fewer than 2,000,000 US patients, conferring 20 years of automatic patent extension
choices.D: Fewer than 50,000 US patients, conferring 10 years of US orphan exclusivity and a guaranteed pediatric PRV

rationale: The US Orphan Drug Act defines a rare disease as affecting fewer than 200,000 people in the United States; FDA Orphan Drug Designation grants 7 years of indication-specific US market exclusivity upon approval, a 100% PDUFA clinical fee waiver ($4,682,003 in FY2026), and a 25% ODTC clinical tax credit (ORPHA:824).
